fixes.explanation: The verse doesn't mention a fine, friend. The LORD says the man “…must be put to death.” (Leviticus 20:2) This is a heavy part of the sermon, so I'll let His words stand just as they are.

That's the group the LORD names: “The people of the land are to stone him.” (Leviticus 20:2) The verse gives this job to the people of the land and names no one else for it. It's a heavy line, so I'll keep to what the verse says.

The priests aren't named in this verse, friend. The LORD says, “The people of the land are to stone him.” (Leviticus 20:2) He hands this job to the people of the land, so that's the group to remember here.
Elders and gates don't show up in this verse, friend. The LORD says, “The people of the land are to stone him.” (Leviticus 20:2) The group He names is the people of the land.

Yes, “family.” The LORD says, “…then I will set My face against that man and his family…” (Leviticus 20:5) So it reaches past the one man to his family too. Verse 5 says this is what follows if the people hide their eyes and don't put the man to death. It's a serious line.

Servants aren't named in this verse, friend. The LORD says He will set His face “…against that man and his family…” (Leviticus 20:5) The verse then goes on to mention “…all who follow him in prostituting themselves with Molech.” The word for the blank is family.

Holy it is. The LORD says, “Consecrate yourselves, therefore, and be holy, because I am the LORD your God.” (Leviticus 20:7) Right after all those serious warnings, He turns to what He wants for them. And the reason He gives is “…because I am the LORD your God.”

Wise is a great thing to be, friend, but it isn't the word the LORD picks here. He says, “Consecrate yourselves, therefore, and be holy…” (Leviticus 20:7) And He gives His reason right away: “…because I am the LORD your God.” The call is to be holy.

This one is true, friend. The LORD says, “And you shall keep My statutes and practice them.” (Leviticus 20:8) So He does tell them to keep His statutes, and to practice them too. Both of those are in the one sentence.

That's the one. The LORD says, “I am the LORD who sanctifies you.” (Leviticus 20:8) To sanctify is to make holy. Just before this, He told them to consecrate themselves and be holy, and here He says He is the One who makes them holy. So they keep His statutes, and He is the One doing the sanctifying.

That phrase isn't in this verse, friend. The LORD says, “I am the LORD who sanctifies you.” (Leviticus 20:8) To sanctify is to make holy. Right after telling them to keep His statutes, He says He is the One who makes them holy.

That's not how He describes Himself in this verse, friend. He says, “I am the LORD who sanctifies you.” (Leviticus 20:8) To sanctify is to make holy. Verse 7 told them to be holy, and here He says He is the One who makes them so.

Dust isn't the wording in this verse, friend. The LORD says, “…so that the land where I am bringing you to live will not vomit you out.” (Leviticus 20:22) The picture He uses is the land vomiting them out. It's a blunt image, and it's the one to remember.

Strength isn't the reason in this verse, friend. The LORD first says, “You must not follow the statutes of the nations I am driving out before you.” (Leviticus 20:23) Then He gives His reason: “Because they did all these things, I abhorred them.” The reason is what the nations did, not how strong they were.

Walled cities don't come up in this verse. The LORD tells Israel not to follow the statutes of the nations, then says, “Because they did all these things, I abhorred them.” (Leviticus 20:23) The reason is the things they did, not anything they built.

This one is true, friend. The LORD says, “But I have told you that you will inherit their land, since I will give it to you as an inheritance…” (Leviticus 20:24) So He does promise them the land of the nations He's driving out. And He says He will give it to them as an inheritance.

That's the LORD's own description: “…a land flowing with milk and honey.” (Leviticus 20:24) He says He will give it to them as an inheritance. So it's a gift He promises, with a rich picture attached.

Wealth isn't what the verse says, friend. The LORD says He is the God “…who has set you apart from the peoples.” (Leviticus 20:24) Being set apart is about being separated from the peoples, not about having more than they do. Verse 26 says what it's for: “…to be My own.” (Leviticus 20:26)

Strength isn't in this verse, friend. The LORD says He is the God “…who has set you apart from the peoples.” (Leviticus 20:24) Set apart means set apart from the peoples, and it's about who they belong to. Verse 26 puts it this way: “…to be My own.” (Leviticus 20:26)

True. The LORD says, “I have set these apart as unclean for you.” (Leviticus 20:25) Right before that, He tells them to distinguish between clean and unclean animals and birds, and not to become contaminated. So the line between them is His, and Israel is told to keep it in view.

That one is false, friend. The verse says nothing about the nations watching. The LORD says, “You are to be holy to Me because I, the LORD, am holy…” (Leviticus 20:26) The nations do appear in the verse, but as the ones He set Israel apart from. His reason is that He is holy.

Messengers isn't the word here, friend. The LORD says, “…and I have set you apart from the nations to be My own.” (Leviticus 20:26) Own means they belong to Him. They're set apart from the nations, and set apart for Him.
